speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; please describe exactly when these symptoms started and what they feel like. REQUEST TEST: Basic metabolic panel, Cardiac enzymes, ECG.

speaker: Doctor
text: The initial workup for metabolic, cardiac, and enzymatic causes is normal. Can you describe the specific quality of your chest pain (e.g., burning, pressure) and whether it is related to eating, and when did the vomiting first begin?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave syndrome (spontaneous esophageal rupture).

The history of forceful vomiting following heavy alcohol consumption, followed by choking, coughing, and chest pain, is a classic presentation for esophageal perforation. Given the severity of the symptoms and the inability to communicate effectively, please prepare for immediate surgical consultation and confirm the diagnosis with a Water-soluble contrast esophagram or CT chest with oral contrast.
